summarySteps: 1. Corporate Hedging ([fact-01]): Strategic derivative execution to neutralize commercial operating exposures, distinct from speculation.
2. Cost-Center Mandate ([fact-02]): Treasuries must be evaluated on risk-reduction efficacy, preventing profit-center speculative hazards.
3. P&G Swap Disasters ([fact-03]): $157 million loss on leveraged CMT and Bundesbank interest rate swaps.
4. Orange County Bankruptcy ([fact-04]): $20B reverse repo leverage on inverse floaters causing $1.7B net loss and Chapter 9 bankruptcy.
5. Metallgesellschaft Contango ([fact-05]): Short-term futures roll yields and backwardation-to-contango shifts draining $1.3B in liquidity.
6. Liquidity vs. Solvency ([fact-07]): Decoupling cash reserves from paper solvency to survive intra-day margin calls.
7. Exotic Derivatives Ban ([fact-09]): Corporate bylaws prohibiting asymmetric leveraged exotics like knock-out options and range accruals.
8. Multi-Factor Stress Testing ([fact-10]): Simulating extreme rate shocks and liquidity freezes ensuring cash buffers withstand 30 days.
bottomTakeaway: Corporate hedging requires strict treasury cost-center governance, avoidance of leveraged repo structures and contango roll drains, and maintenance of unencumbered cash buffers backed by 30-day stress tests ([fact-02], [fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-07], [fact-10]).
